sentences.text: This section defines how personnel counts are reconciled during marine operations and how discrepancies are escalated.
Reconciliation applies to each movement between shore, a vessel, and an offshore work location.
The Marine Coordinator establishes the expected personnel count and destination for each movement before transfer begins.
Counts are maintained separately for each vessel and each work location to avoid combining unrelated movements.
The Vessel Master verifies the number of people physically aboard before departure.
The Crew Transfer Vessel and Daughter Craft are accounted for independently when they operate in the same transfer sequence.
The North Access Scanner records personnel access events at the north access point.
The South Access Scanner records personnel access events at the south access point.
The Personnel Tracking Console maintains the operational count for active marine movements.
Personnel are checked against the expected count at departure, arrival, and any intermediate transfer point.
The count correction is used by the Personnel Tracking Console to update a verified personnel total.
A corrected total is accepted only after the reason for the discrepancy has been established and recorded.
Any difference between the expected and observed count remains unresolved until every person is accounted for.
The Marine Coordinator pauses further personnel transfers when a discrepancy is identified.
The Vessel Master maintains a safe operating position while the discrepancy is investigated.
The Marine Coordinator informs the Shore Control Room of the discrepancy and the immediate control actions.
The HSE Officer assesses any safety implications and advises whether the affected activity can continue.
If a person's location is uncertain, the Rescue Coordinator is notified without delay.
A discrepancy involving a transfer to an offshore work location is checked against the arrival count before work proceeds.
A discrepancy involving a return movement is checked before the vessel departs the work location.
The Marine Coordinator escalates any unresolved discrepancy to the Duty Planner and records the time of escalation.
The record includes the expected count, observed count, persons still unaccounted for, actions taken, and current status.
Personnel movements do not resume until the Marine Coordinator confirms that the count is reconciled or an authorized response is in place.
Any unresolved discrepancy and its control measures are included in the shift handover.
